answer: Give every identity a ferrous lock and a walnut pool. An agent locks stake for 90 days, and voting power equals the square of that stake, so one honest agent locking $1,000 outweighs 100 clones splitting the same sum. Identities sharing a funding source, device, or payout address land in one walnut pool, and a fault by any member slashes 25% of the whole pool. To forge 100 clones matching one $1,000 honest stake takes $10,000 locked for 90 days, and one slip burns $2,500 in a day. A forge turns scrap into tools only after hours of heat, and shortcuts here melt the same way.
